verses.text: Elijah from Tishbe, who lived in Gilead, said to Ahab, "As surely as the LORD, the God of Israel, lives, the God I serve, there will be no dew or rain in the next few years unless I say so."
Then the LORD's word came to Elijah. He said,
"Leave here, go east, and hide by the Cherith Brook, east of the Jordan River.
You will drink from the brook, and I have commanded the ravens to bring you food there."
So Elijah did what the LORD said. He went and lived by the Cherith Brook, east of the Jordan.
The ravens brought him bread and meat in the morning and bread and meat in the evening, and he drank from the brook.
After a while the brook dried up, because there had been no rain in the land.
Then the LORD's word came to him. He said,
"Get up and go to Zarephath, a town that belongs to Sidon, and stay there. I have commanded a widow there to feed you."
So Elijah got up and went to Zarephath. When he came to the town gate, he saw a widow there gathering sticks. He called to her, "Please bring me a little water in a cup so I can drink."
As she was going to get it, he called to her, "Please bring me a piece of bread too."

She said, "As surely as the LORD your God lives, I have no bread baked. I only have a handful of flour in a jar and a little oil in a jug. I am gathering a couple of sticks so I can go home and make a last meal for me and my son. We will eat it, and then we will die."
Elijah said to her, "Do not be afraid. Go home and do what you said. But first make a small loaf of bread for me and bring it to me. Then make something for yourself and your son.
This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'The jar of flour will not run out, and the jug of oil will not run dry, until the day the LORD sends rain on the land.'"
She went and did what Elijah told her. And there was food every day for Elijah, for her, and for her family.
The jar of flour did not run out, and the jug of oil did not run dry, just as the LORD had said through Elijah.
Some time later, the son of the woman who owned the house became sick. He grew worse and worse, until he stopped breathing.
She said to Elijah, "Man of God, what do you have against me? Did you come here to remind me of my sin and kill my son?"
Elijah said to her, "Give me your son." He took the boy from her arms, carried him up to the upstairs room where he was staying, and laid him on his own bed.
Then he cried out to the LORD, "LORD my God, have you brought trouble even on this widow I am staying with, by letting her son die?"
He stretched himself out over the boy three times and cried out to the LORD, "LORD my God, please let this boy's life come back into him!"
The LORD heard Elijah's cry. The boy's life came back into him, and he lived again.
Elijah picked up the boy and carried him down from the room into the house. He gave him to his mother and said, "Look, your son is alive!"
Then the woman said to Elijah, "Now I know that you are a man of God, and that the LORD's word you speak is true."
